entries.title: I Kings 8:1
segments:
Bring up the ark; from mount Zion in the south-west part of Jerusalem, where David lived, to the temple on mount Moriah, an elevation in the east part of the city. 
 
The most costly and splendid temple without the presence and favor of God, is but a dead mass of useless matter; and the most exact and gorgeous forms of worship, without love and faith in the worshippers, are no more pleasing to him than sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal.

entries.title: I Kings 8:2
segments:
The feast; of tabernacles. 
 
  Ethanim; answering to a part of September and October.

entries.title: I Kings 8:4
segments: The tabernacle of the congregation; as this was the peculiar name by which the tabernacle constructed by Moses in the wilderness was known, it is probable that it had been brought from Gibeon, where it was at the beginning of Solomon's reign--
--to be deposited in the temple.  Some, however, suppose that we are here to understand the tabernacle which David had prepared for the ark when he brought it from the house of Obed-edom.

entries.title: I Kings 8:6
segments: Under the wings of the cheribum; the two cherubim of olive-wood that Solomon had placed in the holy of holies,

entries.title: I Kings 8:8
segments: The staves; those by which the ark was borne,

. They were drawn partly out, so that their ends projected into the holy place. 
 
  Unto this day; an expression which the author of the books of Kings seems to have retained from "the book of the acts of Solomon."

entries.title: I Kings 8:10
segments: The cloud; the symbol of God's presence,

. 
 
When the people of God have dedicated to him a house, and assemble in it to worship him in spirit and in truth, they may expect glorious manifestations of his presence, and rich spiritual joys.

entries.title: I Kings 8:17
segments: To every sincere desire for the promotion of his glory and the good of men, God is witness; and whether it can consistently be now granted or not, he will connect it with great results, and bestow upon it gracious and glorious reward.

entries.title: I Kings 8:22
segments: Stood before the altar; he presented himself before the altar, standing with his face towards the congregation, and then kneeled down and spread out his hands as he prayed,

. 
 
Every ruler should be a man of prayer, and on suitable occasions should publicly set the example of acknowledging and adoring God; blessing him for his goodness, and seeking of him those mercies which are needed for rulers and people.

entries.title: I Kings 8:26
segments: Verified; shown to be true, by its fulfilment.

entries.title: I Kings 8:29
segments:
May be open; look with favor. 
 
  Toward; in

entries.title: I Kings 8:31
segments: An oath be laid upon him; this oath he was required to take before the altar.

entries.title: I Kings 8:33
segments: In; toward,

.  The word in the original means in, or toward, according to the connection. 
 
The public calamities of a people are caused by their sins; and repentance, reformation, and earnest supplications to God are his appointed means for their removal.

entries.title: I Kings 8:38
segments: The plague of his own heart; the sorrow that is his own special burden, and which he feels to be the chastisement from God for his sin.

entries.title: I Kings 8:41
segments:
For thy names's sake; on account of what he had heard about God, and for the purpose of worshipping him and sharing in the blessings of his people. 
 
All enlightened and sincere friends of God earnestly desire that the blessings which he bestows on them may be enjoyed by all people, and that for this end he may be revealed to them and they may be taught to worship him in the beauty of holiness.

entries.title: I Kings 8:46
segments: There is no land so distant or dark, and no condition so trying, that men may not think of their sins as the cause of their sorrows, repent of them, from the heart make supplication to God, and in due time receive abundant answers to their prayers.

entries.title: I Kings 8:58
segments: God is the author of the inclination to love and serve him, and no greater blessing is ever bestowed by him on earth, than a disposition to believe his declarations and keep his commandments.

entries.title: I Kings 8:63
segments: A sacrifice of peace-offerings--two and twenty thousand oxen-- twenty thousand sheep; certain prescribed portions of these peace-offerings were burned,
, and from the rest he furnished a feast for the immense multitude of the people assembled from all parts of the land for fourteen days,
.  In this he imitated the example of David when he removed the ark to Zion,
.  Thus was strikingly typified the spiritual feast which a greater than Solomon has provided for all who believe, by the sacrifice of his blood,

entries.title: I Kings 8:65
segments:
The entering in of Hamath; on the north border of Canaan. 
 
Sincere and upright worship of God, and hearty obedience to his commands, is a source of gladness and exceeding joy.  It raises the soul to the highest enjoyment which can be found on earth, and fits it for perfect and endless bliss in heaven.
